territorial_scope.description: Federal rule of the US Department of Health and Human Services applying to developers of certified health IT under the ONC certification program.

evidence.quote: Provide means the action or actions taken by a developer of certified Health IT Modules to make the certified health IT available to its customers

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: HHS final rule amending 45 CFR Part 170 on certified health IT. It updates interoperability, vocabulary and API standards and certification criteria, defines Predictive Decision Support Interventions, and requires developers of such tools in certified Health IT Modules to provide source-attribute information and risk management.
summary.long: HTI-1 is a federal health IT rule that amends Part 170 of Title 45 of the Code of Federal Regulations for developers of health IT seeking ONC certification. It adds definitions, including 'Predictive Decision Support Intervention' and 'Provide', and revises or adds standards in § 170.205 (content exchange, including electronic case reporting), § 170.207 (vocabularies such as SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, and sex, gender identity and sexual orientation codes), § 170.210 (NTP-synchronized clocks), § 170.213 (USCDI v1 and v3) and § 170.215 (FHIR, US Core, SMART and bulk export APIs), with incorporation by reference in § 170.299. It amends the certification criteria in § 170.315, including patient demographics, family health history and decision support interventions. For Predictive DSIs supplied in a certified Health IT Module, § 170.315(b)(11) requires source-attribute information (such as training-data inclusion criteria and fairness and performance measures), access and modification functions, and intervention risk management covering risk analysis, mitigation and governance. Some standard adoptions expire, and some criteria require conformance, on January 1, 2025 or January 1, 2026. The provided text contains no enforcement provisions.

notes: The document is an excerpt of amendatory instructions and regulatory text for 45 CFR part 170 (Instructions 1 to 9). It has no preamble, effective date or consolidated text, so no version or extent is established here. Numbering is garbled in places (e.g., orphaned '( 2)' items in § 170.315(b)(1)(iii) and (b)(11)(iv)(B)); quotes follow the extracted text. Some adoption expiry dates are written two ways: § 170.315(a)(5)(i)(C) and (D) use 'up to and including December 31, 2025', while § 170.207(n)(1), § 170.205(a)(5) and § 170.213(a) use 'expires on January 1, 2026'. The web address in § 170.299(o) appears garbled ('www.Ph.D.sc.org') in the extracted text. The entities list covers only named public bodies and standards organisations that appear in the text; generic health IT developers and Predictive DSI developers are not listed as entities.

definitions.term: ONC certification criteria for health IT

evidence.provision: § 170.102 (definition: ONC certification criteria for health IT; added by Sec. 2)
evidence.quote: ONC certification criteria for health IT means the certification criteria in § 170.315.

evidence.provision: § 170.102 (definition: Predictive Decision Support Intervention or Predictive DSI; added by Sec. 2)
evidence.quote: Predictive Decision Support Intervention or Predictive DSI means technology that supports decision-making based on algorithms or models that derive relationships from training data and then produces an output that results in prediction, classification, recommendation, evaluation, or analysis.
Provide means the action or actions taken by a developer of certified Health IT Modules to make the certified health IT available to its customers.

evidence.provision: § 170.102 (definition: Revised certification criterion (or criteria); added by Sec. 2)
evidence.quote: Revised certification criterion (or criteria) means a certification criterion that meets at least one of the following:

obligations.summary: Certified health IT developers (text: 'health IT developer') must update each Health IT Module certified to a revised criterion and provide the update to customers on the dates set for each criterion and standard. Applies to all criteria in § 170.315.
obligations.applies_from: Dates identified for each revised certification criterion and each applicable standard in 45 CFR part 170 subpart B
obligations.conditional_on: Health IT Module certified to any revised certification criterion (§ 170.102)

evidence.quote: a health IT developer with a Health IT Module certified to any revised certification criterion, as defined in § 170.102, shall update the Health IT Module and shall provide such update to their customers

obligations.summary: Health IT must be able to electronically perform the capabilities listed in § 170.315 in accordance with the applicable adopted standards and implementation specifications.

evidence.quote: Health IT must be able to electronically perform the following capabilities in accordance with applicable standards and implementation specifications adopted in this part.

obligations.summary: Health IT must enable recording of patient race, ethnicity, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity (including declining to specify) under the adopted standards; sex, sexual orientation and gender identity standards apply up to and including December 31, 2025, or the alternative standards named in the text.
obligations.applies_from: Up to and including December 31, 2025 for the sex, sexual orientation and gender identity standards in (C) to (E); the alternative standards are stated without an end date

evidence.quote: Enable sex to be recorded in accordance with the standard specified in § 170.207(n)(1) for the period up to and including December 31, 2025; or § 170.207(n)(2).

obligations.summary: Health IT must enable at least one sex parameter for clinical use, at least one preferred name to use, and at least one pronoun to be recorded, under the adopted standards (§ 170.207(n)(3) and (o)(4)).

evidence.quote: Conformance with this paragraph is required by January 1, 2026.

obligations.summary: Health IT must enable a user to record, change and access a patient's family health history in accordance with the familial concepts or expressions in the adopted standard.

evidence.quote: Enable a user to record, change, and access a patient's family health history

obligations.summary: Interoperability duties under § 170.315(b)(1)-(9): health IT must support the adopted data-class, transition-of-care and prescription standards by stated dates, and must be able to demonstrate correct patient matching for received transition-of-care or referral summaries. Several standard versions are tied to periods ending December 31, 2025 or to later alternative standards.
obligations.applies_from: Time periods up to and including December 31, 2025 for some standard versions; alternative standards stated without an end date
obligations.conditional_on: Receipt of a transition of care/referral summary (for patient matching)

evidence.quote: technology must be able to demonstrate that the transition of care/referral summary received can be properly matched to the correct patient.

obligations.summary: Decision support interventions must occur during user interaction with the technology; a limited set of identified users must be able to configure interventions by role, select evidence-based and predictive interventions, and record and export feedback data in computable format.

evidence.quote: Enable interventions specified in paragraphs (b)(11)(iii) of this section to be configured by a limited set of identified users based on a user's role.

obligations.summary: Source attributes must be supported for evidence-based and Predictive Decision Support Interventions. For predictive interventions these cover developer name, intended use and population, cautioned out-of-scope uses, training data and input features, demographic representativeness, fairness, external validation, performance measures and maintenance schedules.

evidence.quote: Source attributes listed in paragraphs (b)(11)(iv)(A) and (B) of this section must be supported.

obligations.summary: For developer-supplied Predictive Decision Support Interventions, the Health IT Module must let a limited set of identified users access plain-language descriptions of source attributes and indicate when information is unavailable; it must also let identified users record, change and access source attributes.
obligations.conditional_on: Intervention supplied by the health IT developer as part of its Health IT Module

evidence.quote: the Health IT Module must enable a limited set of identified users to access complete and up-to-date plain language descriptions of source attribute information

obligations.summary: Each Predictive Decision Support Intervention supplied by the developer must be subject to analysis of risks and adverse impacts (validity, reliability, robustness, fairness, intelligibility, safety, security, privacy), to risk mitigation practices, and to governance policies and controls covering how data are acquired, managed and used.
obligations.conditional_on: Predictive Decision Support Intervention supplied by the health IT developer as part of its Health IT Module

evidence.quote: The Predictive Decision Support Intervention(s) must be subject to analysis of potential risks and adverse impacts

obligations.summary: Sex must be coded per the adopted SNOMED CT standard; sexual orientation, gender identity and pronouns per the adopted SNOMED CT or LOINC codes and HL7 value sets, with transitional periods ending December 31, 2025 or January 1, 2026 as stated.
obligations.applies_from: Some sub-paragraphs end 31 Dec 2025 or 1 Jan 2026; others have no stated date

evidence.quote: Sex must be coded in accordance with, at a minimum, the version of SNOMED CT

obligations.summary: Social, psychological and behavioral data (financial resource strain, education, stress, depression, physical activity, alcohol use, social connection, intimate partner violence) must be coded per the adopted LOINC standard with the listed LOINC codes and units.

evidence.quote: Financial resource strain must be coded in accordance with, at a minimum, the version of LOINC® codes

obligations.summary: The date and time recorded must use a system clock synchronized by any Network Time Protocol (NTP) standard.

evidence.quote: The date and time recorded utilize a system clock that has been synchronized using any Network Time Protocol (NTP) standard.
